title: The Mac and Cheese My Family Requests Every Single Sunday
description: A reliable, ultra-creamy baked macaroni and cheese recipe with a sharp cheddar blend and a crispy panko crust. The ultimate crowd-pleaser for your next dinner.
storyHeading: Why Everyone Asks for This Recipe
story: Last Sunday, I had twelve people squeezed around my dining table, and this baked macaroni and cheese was the first thing to vanish. It’s my go-to for potlucks because it scales up easily and stays creamy even after sitting out for a bit. During my initial testing, I found that if you boil the elbows for the full package time, they turn to mush once they hit the oven. I now pull mine three minutes early—they should still have a firm bite when you drain them. Also, skip the bagged shredded cheese. The starch they add to prevent clumping stops the sauce from reaching that silky, pull-apart texture we all want. I use a mix of sharp cheddar for the punch and Gruyère for that nutty, rich melt. It’s a heavy-hitter for kids and adults alike, especially with that butter-toasted panko crust providing a much-needed crunch against the velvety cheese sauce.
ingredients: 3 cups extra sharp cheddar cheese, grated by hand
1 cup Gruyère cheese, grated by hand
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375°F and lightly grease a 9x13-inch ceramic or glass baking dish with butter.
Boil the elbow macaroni in a large pot of salted water for about 3 minutes less than the package directions for al dente; the pasta should be slightly undercooked.
In a large heavy-bottomed pot, melt the butter over medium heat and whisk in the flour for 1 minute to cook off the raw flour taste.
Gradually pour in the milk while whisking constantly until the sauce thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon, then stir in the mustard powder and paprika.
Remove the pot from the heat and fold in the hand-grated cheeses until the sauce is completely smooth before tossing in the cooked pasta.

Pour the mixture into your prepared dish, sprinkle the panko mixed with a tablespoon of melted butter over the top, and bake for 25 minutes until the sauce is bubbling and the top is deep golden brown.
proHack: If you are prepping this for a party, make the cheese sauce slightly thinner than you think you need by adding an extra half-cup of milk. The pasta absorbs moisture as it sits, and this prevents the dish from getting tight or dry during transport.
servingIdea: This is heavy, so I usually pair it with a crisp green salad tossed in a sharp lemon vinaigrette or some simple roasted broccoli to cut through the richness.
storage: Store leftovers in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat in the oven at 325°F with a splash of milk to bring the creaminess back, or use the microwave in 30-second bursts.

faqs.question: Can I use pre-shredded cheese to save time?
faqs.answer: I really recommend against it. Pre-shredded cheese is coated in potato starch or cellulose to keep it from sticking in the bag, which makes the baked sauce grainy instead of smooth.

faqs.question: How do I keep the panko from burning?
faqs.answer: Keep an eye on the oven during the last 5 minutes. If it's browning too fast, tent the dish loosely with foil so the cheese keeps bubbling without scorching the crumbs.

faqs.question: Is there a good sub for Gruyère?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. If you can't find it or want to save a few dollars, Monterey Jack or even a mild Provolone provides a similar creamy melt, though you’ll lose a bit of that nutty flavor.
